title: Granularity lower bound for nonzero coefficients
statement: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $k$ be a natural number. Suppose the number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of the corresponding function on the binary cube is at most $2^{k+1}$. For any set $U$ of coordinates whose Fourier coefficient for $f$ is nonzero, the absolute value of that coefficient is at least the Fourier granularity at level $k+1$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
The binary-cube function corresponding to $f$ has at most $2^{k+1}$ nonzero Fourier coefficients
The Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $U$ is nonzero
